title: Multi-Instantons and Exact-WKB Stokes Jumps in Multi-Well Quantum Mechanics
abstract: We study the relation between the exact-WKB Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion of a one-dimensional potential with $N$ equal-depth minima. For a single barrier this relation is the Bogomolny--Zinn-Justin cancellation between the instanton--anti-instanton ambiguity and the Borel ambiguity of perturbation theory, and we extend it to every consecutive barrier interval and to the integration contours themselves. In the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, we derive the quasi-zero mode integral over the instanton separations from the Euclidean path integral and reduce it to Gamma and Hankel periods. With the local Weber level function of each well and one normalization per well fixed by the local Weber connection matrix, these periods reproduce the two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients. The two lateral contours of each instanton--anti-instanton separation differ by exactly one Hankel cycle, and this linear Picard--Lefschetz relation reproduces the Stokes jump of the connected coefficient. A numerical solution of the Schrödinger equation for a symmetric triple well confirms the resulting two-barrier level splitting. At higher fixed grade, the map from ordered event sequences to normalized scalar coefficient products is not one-to-one. At leading dilute order the scalar weight of a closed event sequence depends only on the numbers of barrier crossings, $\mathcal I\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs, and $\mathcal I\mathcal I$/$\bar{\mathcal I}\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs. We construct two inequivalent grade-six triple-well event sequences with the same product of local Weber amplitudes, which embed in every potential with $N\ge3$ wells. Our results hold within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.
summary: This theoretical paper connects the semiclassical WKB approximation to the path integral formalism by studying multi-instanton contributions in multi-well potentials. It shows that the Stokes phenomenon, a key feature of WKB theory, is mathematically reproduced by analyzing the quasi-zero mode integral derived from the instanton action. This provides a deep, rigorous link between different mathematical descriptions of quantum tunneling.
main_problem: The paper investigates the deep mathematical relationship between the exact-WKB Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion in quantum mechanics.
main_result: It establishes that the Stokes jump is reproduced by a linear Picard-Lefschetz relation derived from the quasi-zero mode integral, which reduces to Gamma and Hankel periods.
method: The authors employ advanced techniques combining the exact-WKB method, path integrals over instanton events, and Picard-Lefschetz theory.
model_or_system: The study focuses on one-dimensional quantum systems described by a potential with $N$ equal-depth minima (multi-well quantum mechanics).
key_observables: Stokes jumps, two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients, and the spectral splitting of the ground-state doublet.
important_parameters: The analysis is performed in the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, involving parameters like $\hbar$ and the number of wells $N$.
main_assumptions: The results are derived within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.
figures_summary: A numerical solution for a symmetric triple well confirms the theoretically derived two-barrier level splitting.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the foundational case of a single barrier (relating to Bogomolny-Zinn-Justin cancellation) to the general multi-well case, deriving the quasi-zero mode integral and analyzing the structure of event sequences at higher fixed grades.
why_interesting: The connection between nonperturbative instanton calculus (path integrals) and semiclassical quantization conditions (WKB/Stokes phenomena) is fundamental to understanding tunneling and spectral properties in complex quantum systems.
